title: A good-faith criticism safe harbour protects dissent and whistleblowing from the inflammatory-language breach
content:
The first Tier 2 breach listed at A.1.6.6.1.2 is "unsubstantiated public accusations against governance participants and inflammatory language directed at governance participants or processes that does not constitute good-faith criticism." Because Tier 2 means immediate derecognition, that clause is dangerously broad on its own — nearly any forceful criticism of a facilitator could be characterized as inflammatory by the person being criticized, who in this system is also often the adjudicator.

A.1.6.6.1.2.0.3.1 supplies the limiting definition. Good-faith criticism is criticism that "(a) is framed in neutral or professional terms, (b) includes supporting facts or is clearly identified as opinion, and (c) does not constitute a personal attack." And it states the protection explicitly: "Good-faith criticism of governance decisions, processes, or participants is not a Tier 2 breach. This safe harbor protects legitimate governance discourse including dissent, whistleblowing, and strong disagreement."

The three-part test is well-constructed because each element is about *form*, not *content*. Nothing here limits what may be alleged or how severe the criticism may be — only that it be professionally framed, evidenced or honestly labelled as opinion, and directed at conduct rather than persons. A delegate can therefore accuse the Core Facilitator of serious misalignment without breaching, provided they do so with facts and without invective.

The (b) clause is the cleverest part: it offers two routes to compliance. Have supporting facts, *or* say plainly that you are speculating. That preserves the ability to raise a suspicion one cannot yet prove — which is exactly the whistleblower's position, and exactly what the surrounding regime needs, since AC accountability depends on community reports (A.1.6.6.0.4.1).

The residual risk is that the safe harbour is applied by the same role that criticism most often targets, with recusal (A.1.5.9.5) as the only structural check.
description: A.1.6.6.1.2.0.3.1 defines a three-part test — neutral framing, supporting facts or labelled opinion, no personal attack — and states the safe harbour covers strong disagreement.
